rv.q: She makes one mistake, and the whole weight of the patriarchal establishment lands on her shoulders. Still, with so many targets for its fury, this story delivers a generalised bludgeoning, rather than a knockout blow. There’s something so exhaustingly bleak about the way this narrative unfolds.

One of the biggest stars of the evening is Rob Jones’ beautiful set design with its meticulously timed and choreographed transitions which add atmosphere and contrast to proceedings in Director Blanche McIntyre’s splendid production.
But it's a tense and engrossing evening and a wonder to spend it with Duff, the kind of actor you could watch forever.

When asked to clarify what he said, Robson being in a state of shock at the sudden insult, repeated it. Robson challenged him further and she tried to find out the boy’s name from other pupils also at the station, but the train pulled in and in the melee of people disembarking and embarking the reply didn’t register with her.
Duff does her very best with the contrived material... Still, it is not enough to find a real sense of reasoning through this work.

cn.t: Anne-Marie Duff delivers a powerhouse performance in this simple yet twisty drama about a woman's life derailing after a train station incident, though critics are divided on the play's overall impact.

ru.inst: Tickets released Fridays at 1 PM via the National Theatre website (random queue).
